 Rupesh Sonar on Anuj Thakur’s demise: I met him 10 days ago; he was talking about a comeback

 Print Casting director Rupesh Sonar remembers the late actor, Anuj Thakur, as a cheerful, respectful and helpful person and a younger brother. On Friday, October 30, the television industry learnt of the untimely demise of actor Anuj Thakur, who was in his 30s. His friend and casting director Rupesh Sonar shared the news in an Instagram post, leaving those who knew the actor shocked. Paying tribute to Anuj, Rupesh wrote, “I still can’t believe that you are no longer with us. You were not just a friend but like a little brother to me. We had so many projects planned together, and I still remember witnessing your struggles during your initial days and seeing your journey. Life is truly unpredictable. It’s heartbreaking to accept that you are gone so soon. This news feels unreal. You will always be remembered, brother. Rest in peace.” Anuj, who featured in shows such as Dhoom Machao Dhoom, Bandhan Saath Janmon Ka, Beend Banoonga Ghodi Chadhunga and Mahisagar, passed away on October 27. For Rupesh, who had known him since 2008 and worked with him on several shows, the news was particularly difficult to come to terms with, especially since their last meeting was just 10 days before his death. Sharing how he learnt about Anuj’s passing and subsequently met his family to understand what had happened, Rupesh says, “On Friday, at around 8.30 pm, I received a call from a common friend informing me about Anuj’s demise. I couldn’t believe it because I had met him just 10 days earlier. I was shocked to hear that he had gone to sleep at night and never woke up. I couldn’t understand what could have happened. I spoke to his brother, who was not in a position to speak much. So, I went to meet his family, including his mother and brother, on Saturday. That’s when I was told that Anuj had suffered a seizure and passed away during the episode.” He adds, “Anuj was an early riser. He would wake up at 4.30 am every day and follow his routine, which included fitness and jogging. However, that morning, he didn’t get up. His alarm went off at 4.30 am, and when his mother went to his room to wake him, she found that he had passed away.” Having known Anuj for nearly 17 years, Rupesh remembers him as more than a colleague. Their association began with Bandhan Saath Janmon Ka in 2008, and they went on to work together on several shows, including Beend Banoonga Ghodi Chadhunga. Their last meeting, just 10 days before Anuj’s death, also brought up the subject of his return to acting. Remembering his enthusiasm and the warmth with which he treated people, Rupesh says, “I have known Anuj since 2008, when we worked together on our first show, Bandhan Saath Janmon Ka. We did several shows together after that. It is very difficult to accept that he is no more. I met him just 10 days ago, and he was talking about making a comeback. His enthusiasm was exactly the same as it had been in 2008. He always spoke respectfully to everyone and treated people with dignity. He was generous, cheerful and helpful. He was a wonderful person and like a younger brother to me. I still cannot understand why he had to leave us so soon.” Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. Download the TOI app.
